title: Narrow the union
summary: Use TypeScript narrowing to handle strings and numbers safely.

scenario.briefing: Order identifiers can arrive as strings or numbers. A formatter calls string methods without checking, so numeric ids crash. Narrow the union and format both cases.

objectives.description: Branch on the runtime type of a union value.
Check understanding through the remaining explanation and transfer evidence.

hints: Numbers become text with String(value) or template literals.
Trim and uppercase strings, and format numbers as-is.
Use typeof; return `ID-${typeof value === "string" ? value.trim().toUpperCase() : value}`.

misconceptions.description: Asserting a type instead of checking the value.
misconceptions.testDescription: A number is formatted as digits.
misconceptions.feedback: A type assertion does not change the runtime value. Use a typeof check so both branches are safe.

misconceptions.description: Calling string methods on a union without narrowing.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Calling trim on a number throws before any branch can format it.
misconceptions.feedback: trim exists only on strings. Narrow the union before calling string methods.

misconceptions.description: Believing a type assertion changes the runtime value.
misconceptions.feedback: Assertions are erased during compilation. Only runtime checks narrow a value safely.

sections.title: Unions describe alternatives
sections.body: A value typed string | number can be either at runtime. TypeScript allows only operations valid for every member until code narrows the type. typeof checks, property checks, and equality checks create narrowed branches.

sections.title: Narrowing is runtime truth
sections.body: A type assertion tells the compiler to believe something; it does not verify the value. Narrowing inspects the actual value and keeps both branches safe. This distinction matters at boundaries where data arrives from JSON.

vocabulary.definition: A type that permits one of several alternatives.
Refining a union to a specific member through checks.
A compile-time claim that does not change runtime behavior.
